summary: Two unidentified Colorado snowmobilers (ages 58 and 65, from Deer Trail and Thornton) searching for Forrest Fenn's hidden treasure set out from the Denver area March 17, rented snowmobiles at Dinosaur National Monument, and proceeded into the wilderness Wednesday; when snow ran out they pressed on foot with only candy bars and water. Moffat County Sheriff's Office requested Dinosaur National Monument ranger help Thursday; the pair was located by helicopter surveillance Saturday in a remote area of the monument near the Utah/Colorado border — the 58-year-old was found deceased and the 65-year-old was found alive and flown by helicopter to a hospital. The men were found within five miles of a site where they had previously been rescued by emergency crews on Feb. 29.
location: Wild Mountain area, northwest boundary of Dinosaur National Monument, Utah/Colorado border
responding_agency: Moffat County Sheriff's Office; Dinosaur National Monument rangers
